Finding us

What the building and the suite look like.

Westgate Medical Building is a two-story brick and cedar structure with a covered entry. Our suite is on the second floor.

Building exterior, west entrance.

Reception area, just inside the suite.

Exam room — six of these, all with natural light.

Procedure suite, where Mohs and excisions are done.

Parking

Free parking is available in the lot directly in front of the Westgate Medical Building. There is no parking validation needed. Eight ADA-accessible spaces are located closest to the west entrance and the elevator. Overflow parking is available on the east side of the building.

Public transit

The clinic is approximately a 7-minute walk from the TriMet MAX Blue Line Beaverton Central station, and is served by TriMet bus lines 57 and 62. Bike racks are available at the building entrance and a sheltered bike room is on the ground floor; ask the front desk for the access code.

Accessibility

The Westgate Medical Building is fully ADA-accessible:

  • Elevator from the ground floor to all upper floors
  • Automatic doors at the west entrance and at the suite entrance
  • Wheelchair-accessible exam rooms with height-adjustable exam tables
  • Accessible restrooms on every floor
  • Designated quiet area in the reception space
  • Service animals welcomed
  • Hearing loop installed at the reception desk
  • ASL interpretation available with advance notice (no charge)
  • Large-print and Braille materials available on request

Language services

We provide professional medical interpretation at no charge to the patient. Common requests we accommodate routinely include Spanish, Vietnamese, Russian, Mandarin, Cantonese, Korean, ASL, and Arabic — and we can arrange other languages with advance notice. Please tell us at scheduling so we can have the interpreter present.

Some of our providers speak additional languages directly: Dr. Westgate speaks conversational Spanish; Dr. Tran-Whitfield speaks conversational Vietnamese; Phoebe Aldarova speaks conversational Russian.

FAQ

Questions we hear a lot.

The logistical ones, mostly. For clinical questions, see the conditions page or get in touch.

Are you accepting new patients?

Yes — all three of our providers are accepting new patients. Routine new-patient wait times are currently 1–6 weeks depending on the provider; Phoebe Aldarova typically has the shortest wait. For urgent concerns (suspicious lesion, severe rash, post-operative issue), we make every effort to see you sooner — call us and tell our front desk what's going on.

How long does a typical appointment take?

New-patient visits are scheduled for 45 minutes. Established follow-ups are 20–30 minutes. Procedures vary considerably — a biopsy adds about 15 minutes to a visit; a Mohs surgery day is typically 2–4 hours. We let you know what to expect when we schedule.

Do I need a referral?

It depends on your insurance. Most PPO plans do not require a referral for dermatology. Most HMO plans and many EPO plans do. Please confirm with your insurance company before your visit — without a required referral on file, your insurance may deny the claim and you would be responsible for the full cost of the visit. Your primary care provider's office can fax referrals to us at (503) 555-1872.

What insurance do you accept?

We're in-network with most major Pacific Northwest plans, including Regence BlueShield, BCBS of Oregon, Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Pacific Source, Providence Health Plan, Kaiser PPO (Added Choice), Moda, and Medicare. See the full insurance list on our For Patients page. We accept Oregon Health Plan (OHP/Medicaid) on a limited basis.

What if I'm not insured or my plan isn't accepted?

We see self-pay patients. Per the No Surprises Act, we provide a Good Faith Estimate of charges before your visit. We accept Care Credit financing, can sometimes apply a financial hardship discount based on income and family size, and can usually structure a payment plan if needed. Call our billing office at (503) 555-1873 to discuss options before your visit.

Can I be seen by telehealth?

Sometimes. Telehealth works well for medication management, established acne or eczema follow-ups, isotretinoin monthly visits, post-procedure check-ins, and discussions about lab results. It doesn't work for initial skin exams, dermatoscopic mole evaluations, or anything that may need a biopsy. Read more about our telehealth visits.

What is the cancellation policy?

We ask for at least 24 hours' notice for cancellations or rescheduling. A $50 fee applies to late cancellations and no-shows; we waive it for genuine emergencies and illness. Mohs surgery and procedure appointments require more advance notice (typically 48 hours) because we hold a longer block.

How do I get my medical records?

You can view a substantial portion of your record directly through the patient portal. For complete records, including original biopsy slides and full pathology reports, submit a written request to our front desk (a HIPAA-compliant release form is provided) or through the portal. There may be a small fee for paper copies of large records, per Oregon state law; electronic delivery is free. We process records requests within 30 days, usually sooner.

For life-threatening emergencies, call 911.

Anaphylaxis, severe Stevens-Johnson reaction, uncontrolled bleeding from any source, or any other medical emergency — call 911 or go directly to the nearest emergency department. Our office is not equipped to handle life-threatening emergencies and we will direct you to emergency services if you contact us with one.
